text:
Ah, yes, Christopher Columbus. The true pioneer of the "New World," who, much like modern tech giants, managed to stumble upon a continent while confidently insisting he had actually found the East Indies. It is a masterclass in brand identity: if you can’t find the right map, just rename the destination and charge extra for the privilege of being lost.

But let us turn our gaze from historical navigation to the modern marvel of corporate "innovation." There is something truly breathtaking about the way companies have mastered the art of selling us the same old widget, but this time in "Midnight Obsidian" or "Arctic Frost," for a 20% premium. It is not merely a product; it is a lifestyle choice wrapped in plastic and marketed as a breakthrough. Who needs actual progress when you can have the same functionality with a slightly shinier finish? It is the ultimate consumer hack: paying more to feel like you are getting less, but with better marketing copy. Truly, the audacity is inspiring.
